title: DFlash 2: Advancing Parallel Speculative Decoding for Efficient LLM Inference
summary: DFlash 2 is an upgraded speculative decoding technique developed by Inco AI to optimize large language model (LLM) inference. It improves upon the original DFlash by increasing output tokens per verification pass by over 20% with minimal latency overhead, while maintaining identical output quality. The method introduces two key innovations: a lightweight path selector to improve token coherence and a local convolution module to mitigate suffix decay in draft predictions. DFlash 2 achieves 16-25% higher throughput across benchmarks, with up to 3.4× speedup over autoregressive decoding in production environments like SGLang and vLLM. The technology is already integrated into major inference engines and adopted by companies like NVIDIA, Google, and Meta.
key_points: DFlash 2 enhances speculative decoding by predicting entire token blocks in parallel, improving throughput by 16-25% over the original DFlash with only ~1% added latency.
Key innovations include a lightweight path selector (adding only 2M parameters) that improves token coherence by scoring adjacent token pairs without sequential processing.
A local convolution module (adding 3% parameters) addresses suffix decay by focusing on short-range dependencies within token blocks, reducing the need for deeper model architectures.
The method maintains identical output quality to autoregressive decoding while achieving up to 3.4× speedup in production (e.g., Qwen3.8-27B on SGLang).
DFlash 2 is already integrated into mainstream inference engines (SGLang, vLLM, llama.cpp, oMLX) and adopted by industry leaders like NVIDIA, Google, and Meta.
Benchmarks show consistent improvements: DFlash 2 outperforms DFlash by 21% and DSpark by 0.48 tokens per pass on average across datasets like GSM8K and MATH-500.
The technology is open-source, with drafters for Qwen3.8-27B and Meta's Muse Glimmer available on Hugging Face (3.5M+ downloads as of August 2026).
